specPoints.text: understand that plants can reproduce asexually by natural methods (illustrated by runners) and by artificial methods (illustrated by cuttings)

primer.text: Gardeners cheat time: a strawberry patch doubles itself without a single seed, and a prized rose is copied stem by stem. This note covers both routes — the runner, a plant's own side branch that roots itself, and the cutting, a human-operated clone kit that turns one good plant into many identical ones.

lessons.title: Cloning Without a Seed
lessons.opening: Asexual reproduction in plants needs one parent only: no gametes meet, no pollen flies, and every offspring is a genetic clone of that parent, whether the plant grows the new individual itself or a gardener helps.
keyPoints: Asexual reproduction involves one parent only.
All offspring are exact genetic copies of the parent — they are clones.
The cloning can happen naturally, as with runners, or artificially, as with cuttings.

low.restatement: One parent, no gametes, identical offspring; the plant copies itself by growing new shoots that become new plants.
low.analogy: Photocopying a page instead of retyping it: the copy matches the original exactly.
low.examPointer: Remember the contrast set: natural = runners, artificial = cuttings.

medium.restatement: Because no fertilisation occurs, mitosis alone builds the new plant, so the genome is passed on unshuffled; the offspring differ from the parent only by mutation, if at all.
medium.analogy: A franchise opening identical branches from one blueprint.
medium.examPointer: Use the word clone explicitly — the mark scheme looks for genetically identical offspring.

check.stem: How many parents does asexual reproduction in plants involve?

options.text: One
options.explanation: Correct — this follows directly from the definition.

options.text: Two
options.explanation: Two parents belong to sexual reproduction.

options.text: Three or more
options.explanation: No reproduction mode needs three parents.

options.text: None at all
options.explanation: One parent supplies all the genetic material.

check.stem: What is the genetic relationship between a plantlet grown from a runner and its parent?

options.text: The plantlet is a genetically identical clone of the parent
options.explanation: Yes — the mechanism works exactly this way.

options.text: It shares half its genes with the parent
options.explanation: Half-share inheritance happens with gametes, which asexual reproduction avoids.

options.text: It has twice the parent's chromosomes
options.explanation: Chromosome number stays the same in mitotic cloning.

options.text: It is a different species
options.explanation: The offspring stay within the parent's species.

check.stem: Which statement about asexual reproduction in plants is correct?

options.text: It can occur naturally or be controlled artificially by humans
options.explanation: Correct — this matches the account taught above.

options.text: It always requires human help
options.explanation: Runners spread with no gardener at all.

options.text: It always involves gamete fusion
options.explanation: Fusion of gametes is sexual, not asexual.

options.text: It produces varied offspring for selection
options.explanation: Variation is the hallmark of sexual reproduction.

check.stem: Why do clones of a healthy parent usually grow into healthy adult plants?

options.text: They carry exactly the parent's genome, including its favourable alleles
options.explanation: Right — this is the account the lesson teaches.

options.text: They shuffle genes to escape disease
options.explanation: No shuffling happens without gametes.

options.text: They mutate on purpose to improve
options.explanation: Mutations are random, not purposeful.

options.text: They borrow genes from neighbouring plants
options.explanation: Cloning imports no foreign genes.

check.stem: A farmer wants a field of potato plants exactly like this year's best performer. Which reproduction route fits?

options.text: Asexual reproduction, cloning the performer vegetatively
options.explanation: Right — the other options each misplace a concept.

options.text: Sexual reproduction via seed
options.explanation: Seed offspring recombine genes and vary.

options.text: Waiting for natural mutation
options.explanation: Mutation is random and cannot target quality.

options.text: Crossing with a wild relative
options.explanation: Crossing adds foreign alleles and variation.

check.stem: State what all offspring of asexual plant reproduction are, relative to the parent.
check.modelAnswer: They are exact genetic copies of the parent plant — clones that are genetically identical.

check.stem: Name the natural and the artificial method of asexual reproduction in plants.
check.modelAnswer: The natural method is runners and the artificial method is cuttings.

check.stem: Explain why asexual reproduction produces no genetic variation among the offspring.
check.modelAnswer: Only one parent contributes and no gametes fuse, so mitosis copies the single genome unchanged and every offspring inherits an identical set of alleles.

check.stem: A nursery sells a rose variety that cannot breed true from seed. Explain how cuttings solve this.
check.modelAnswer: Cuttings are cloned from the parent plant, so each new rose keeps the exact allele combination that made the variety valuable, with no seed variation.

lessons.title: Runners and Cuttings
sourceHeadings: Natural asexual reproduction in plants – runners
Artificial asexual reproduction in plants – cuttings
lessons.opening: Runners and cuttings both end in cloned plants, but one is grown by the plant itself and one is assembled by a gardener: a runner is a sideways stem carrying plantlets that root where they touch soil, while a cutting is a sliced stem, often dipped in rooting powder, that grows its own roots.
keyPoints: Runners are horizontal stems growing sideways from the parent with small plantlets at their ends.
Plantlets grow roots once they touch the soil and become independent new plants.
Cuttings are sections cut from good parent plants, usually bearing a new bud.
A cutting can root in water or soil, sometimes dipped in rooting powder first.
Cloning by cuttings is cheap and quick for gardeners.

low.restatement: The plant sends out a sideways stem that roots itself; the gardener snips a stem and roots it in water or soil.
low.analogy: One method is the plant laying its own railway sleepers; the other is the gardener laying them for it.
low.examPointer: Quote runner for natural and cutting for artificial — the spec names both illustrations.

medium.restatement: Both routes work because stems carry meristem tissue able to sprout roots; rooting powder simply adds plant growth regulators that push root development along faster.
medium.analogy: A cutting with rooting powder is a stem given a head start on its root apprenticeship.
medium.examPointer: Mention the bud on the cutting and the rooting powder option — both score points in method questions.

check.stem: What is a runner in plant reproduction?

options.text: A horizontal stem growing sideways from the parent that carries small plantlets
options.explanation: Correct — this follows directly from the definition.

options.text: A vertical flower stalk reaching for light
options.explanation: Runners run sideways along the ground.

options.text: A root that stores food over winter
options.explanation: Storage roots are food organs, not cloning stems.

options.text: A seed dispersed by the wind
options.explanation: Runner reproduction never makes seeds.

check.stem: When does a plantlet on a runner become an independent plant?

options.text: Once it touches the soil and grows its own roots
options.explanation: Yes — the mechanism works exactly this way.

options.text: As soon as the runner forms
options.explanation: Forming alone is not enough; roots must grow.

options.text: After the parent dies
options.explanation: The plantlet roots while the parent lives.

options.text: When an insect pollinates it
options.explanation: Pollination plays no part in asexual cloning.

check.stem: Which piece of the cutting method encourages new root growth chemically?

options.text: Dipping the stem into rooting powder containing plant growth regulators
options.explanation: Correct — this matches the account taught above.

options.text: Watering the leaves daily
options.explanation: Leaf watering does not trigger roots.

options.text: Removing all buds from the stem
options.explanation: Cuttings keep a new bud; buds matter.

options.text: Sealing the cut with wax
options.explanation: Sealing blocks the stem rather than rooting it.

check.stem: Why do gardeners take cuttings from the healthiest, best-looking parent plants?

options.text: The clone keeps the parent's genes, so good qualities pass on unchanged
options.explanation: Right — this is the account the lesson teaches.

options.text: Weak parents root faster
options.explanation: Health does not reverse rooting success.

options.text: Cuttings from weak plants mutate better
options.explanation: Mutation is random and undesirable here.

options.text: Strong stems hold more water only
options.explanation: Water holding is not the genetic point.

check.stem: A strawberry plant spreads a runner across a bed and three plantlets root. How do the four plants compare genetically?

options.text: All four are genetically identical clones of one another
options.explanation: Right — the other options each misplace a concept.

options.text: Each plantlet mixes genes differently
options.explanation: No gametes fused, so nothing mixes.

options.text: The parent differs from its plantlets
options.explanation: Mitotic copying keeps them identical.

options.text: They share exactly half their genes
options.explanation: Half-sharing belongs to sexual reproduction.

check.stem: Describe what happens to the plantlets at the end of a runner.
check.modelAnswer: Once the plantlets touch the soil they grow roots and become independent new plants.

check.stem: State where a cutting can be placed so that new roots grow.
check.modelAnswer: A cutting roots either in water, waiting for new roots to sprout, or straight into soil.

check.stem: Explain why cuttings let gardeners clone plants cheaply and quickly.
check.modelAnswer: A cutting is a small section of an existing plant that roots with little equipment, and because it is a clone it reaches sale-ready without the slow variation of seed growing.

check.stem: A gardener wants twenty identical geraniums from one prized plant. Outline the steps using the artificial method.
check.modelAnswer: Cut stem sections bearing new buds from the prized plant, optionally dip the stems in rooting powder, place them in water or soil until roots grow, then plant out twenty genetically identical geraniums.

glossary.definition: A horizontal stem growing sideways from a parent plant, carrying plantlets that root independently.
A tiny new plant formed at the end of a runner, genetically identical to the parent.
A section of stem cut from a parent plant and grown into a new clone.
Powder containing plant growth regulators that encourage a cutting to grow roots.
